issues.legal_issue: An endowment for a family deity is private rather than public when the evidence shows that worship and management remained the concern of the family and the public was not given a right to worship.
material_facts: The deity had been installed in the family home by the testator’s parents and had long been worshipped by the family.
The testator’s will entrusted management and worship to family members and provided for a successor to be selected through the family’s arrangement after their deaths.
The evidence showed that the family, not the public, had performed the regular worship, and that the public had not been allowed to participate in worship as of right.
The will did not provide for public worship or public management, and the evidence did not show that the endowment had acquired a public character.
issues.conclusion: The endowment was private, so it was not subject to the Bihar Hindu Religious Trusts Act, 1950.
issues.legal_principle: The character of an endowment is determined from the instrument creating it, the dealings of the public, and the conduct and habits of those visiting the temple. Dedication to the public is not readily inferred merely from public access or an idol’s popularity; the relevant distinction is whether the beneficiaries are an identified family or the general body of worshippers. The Court applied Babu Bhagwan Din v. Gir Har Saroop (67 I.A. 1), and distinguished Deoki Nandan v. Murlidhar ([1961] 3 S.C.R. 220) and Swami Saligramacharya v. Raghavacharya (Civil Appeal No. 645 of 1964, decided 4 November 1965). The dispute concerned the applicability of the Bihar Hindu Religious Trusts Act, 1950; no specific provision of that Act was construed.

rule.if: religious_endowment_classification_dispute and family_deity_preceded_dedication and family_performed_regular_worship and public_worship_as_of_right_absent and family_retained_management

predicates.religious_endowment_classification_dispu: The proceeding concerns whether a religious endowment is public or private.
predicates.family_deity_preceded_dedication: The deity had been worshipped as a family deity before the endowment was created.
predicates.family_performed_regular_worship: Members of the family performed the regular worship of the deity.
predicates.public_worship_as_of_right_absent: The public was not shown to have a right to participate in worship at the shrine.
predicates.family_retained_management: The instrument creating the endowment entrusted its continuing management to family members or to a successor appointed through the family’s arrangement.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns the character of a religious endowment and the deity was previously a family deity, the family performed regular worship, the public had no right to worship, and the family retained management, the endowment is private.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for tax exemption on income devoted to charitable or religious purposes does not by itself establish that an endowment is public.
material_facts: A document recorded that exemption had been claimed for income set apart for charitable and religious purposes under the endowment.
The evidence and the instrument creating the endowment showed a family deity and family worship, without establishing a public right to worship or public management.
The claim for exemption could have been made to save income from tax and was not decisive of the endowment’s character.
issues.conclusion: The tax-exemption claim did not establish that the endowment was public; its character had to be determined from the creating instrument, public dealings, and the conduct and habits of temple visitors.
issues.legal_principle: The nature of an endowment is determined from the tenor of the document creating it, the dealings of the public, and the conduct and habits of people visiting the temple. A claim for exemption from income tax or agricultural income tax is not decisive because it may have been motivated by a desire to save income. The Court referred to Babu Bhagwan Din v. Gir Har Saroop (67 I.A. 1).

predicates.religious_endowment_classification_dispu: The proceeding concerns whether a religious endowment is public or private.
predicates.tax_exemption_claimed: A person responsible for the endowment claimed tax exemption for income devoted to charitable or religious purposes.

issues.definition: In a dispute over whether a religious endowment is public or private, a tax-exemption claim does not by itself determine that character.
